en.headline: CFS urges public not to eat three French cheese batches over Listeria risk
en.dek: Three batches of Brie-style cheese from the Paturages Comtois brand are under recall after a European alert; importers have stopped sales and begun recalls.
body: The Centre for Food Safety today urged the public not to consume three batches of French cheese possibly contaminated with Listeria monocytogenes. The products are Brie 3kg 50%, Brie 60% 1kg Grand Export and Pointe De Brie 180g, all under the Paturages Comtois brand.

The CFS received a notification through the European Commission’s Rapid Alert System. A preliminary investigation confirmed the three importers had brought the affected batches into Hong Kong. The importers have stopped sales, removed the products from shelves and initiated recalls.

Listeria can cause mild symptoms in healthy people but may lead to serious complications in newborns, the elderly and those with weakened immunity. Pregnant women are advised to avoid high-risk ready-to-eat soft cheeses or ensure they are thoroughly cooked.

zh.headline: 食安中心籲勿食用三批次法國芝士 疑受李斯特菌污染
zh.dek: 三款Paturages Comtois品牌布里芝士因歐盟警報被回收，入口商已停售並展開回收。
body: 食物安全中心今日呼籲市民不要食用三批次可能受李斯特菌污染的法國芝士，產品為Paturages Comtois品牌的Brie 3kg 50%、Brie 60% 1kg Grand Export及Pointe De Brie 180g。
中心接獲歐盟快速警報系統通知後展開初步調查，確認三名入口商曾進口受影響批次。入口商已停止銷售、從貨架移除有關產品並按指示展開回收。
李斯特菌可令健康人士出現輕微症狀，但對初生嬰兒、長者及免疫力較弱人士可能引起嚴重併發症。孕婦應避免高風險的即食軟芝士，或徹底煮熟後才食用。
